audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may treat required or tax-leaking foreign cash as distributable surplus
audit_findings.magnitude: $35.705 million of the $42.088 million cash bridge is held by foreign subsidiaries; complete exclusion would reduce value by $2.08 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any nondistributable operating cash or repatriation tax reduces the cash added in the equity bridge dollar for dollar.
audit_findings.evidence: Of the $40,705 cash and cash equivalents on hand at December 31, 2025, $36,662 was located at our foreign subsidiaries and may be subject to withholding tax if repatriated to the U.S.
audit_findings.explanation: The foreign location is demonstrated, but the amount required locally or lost to tax is unresolved. Even the conservative bound of excluding all $35.705 million of foreign cash lowers base value from $28.14 to about $26.06 per share and bull value from $32.76 to about $30.68, leaving every scenario far below the $94.62 market price. It therefore cannot change the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 2026 cash-by-jurisdiction schedule, minimum operating-cash analysis, repatriation restrictions, and incremental withholding-tax calculation; adjust only the bridge amount shown to be unavailable.

audit_findings.title: A subjective inventory reserve could overstate the owner-earnings numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed sensitivity is a $0.850 million reduction in 2025 net income for each 1% write-down of the $109.198 million year-end inventory; actual reserve shortfall is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An inadequate reserve understates cost of goods sold and overstates reported earnings and the historical OE observations used to derive the trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: We identified the estimate of obsolete or excess inventory, as well as inventory that is not of saleable quality, as a critical audit matter because of the significant amount of judgment required by management when evaluating the assumptions for item specific estimates about the timing or level of demand for a specific part.
audit_findings.explanation: The judgment and exposure are demonstrated, but no reserve deficiency or misstatement is demonstrated. The auditor tested the estimate, the financial statements received an unqualified opinion, and management reported that historical adjustments were adequate; those facts do not eliminate the possibility of a shortfall. Inventory subsequently increased to $117.908 million while demand remained mixed, but the record provides no aging or reserve-coverage data from which materiality can be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain inventory aging and gross reserve balances by product, compare forecasts with subsequent sales and cancellations, identify post-year-end write-downs, and rerun the OE history and log-trend anchor for any supported after-tax reserve correction.

audit_findings.title: Scenario growth could require acquisition spending excluded from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Future acquisition spending is unquantified; modeled equity value is $68 million higher at 3% growth and $148 million higher at 6% growth than at 0% growth
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquisition-dependent growth raises the modeled growth rate while acquisition consideration remains outside OE, overstating operating value under a fixed-perimeter valuation.
audit_findings.evidence: Acquisitions are part of our strategic growth plans.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a forward-looking funding risk, not a demonstrated omission from historical OE. Filed organic revenue growth of 3.2% in 2025 and 5.1% for the first half of 2026 indicates that recent growth did not require acquisitions, but it does not establish that 3%-6% long-term OE growth can be sustained organically. No future transaction or acquisition cost is presently identified.
audit_findings.action: Track fixed-perimeter organic OE rather than revenue, reconcile organic growth to reinvestment already charged in OE, and rerun any scenario shown to require acquisitions with the associated cash consideration deducted or with a lower organic growth rate.

audit_findings.title: A genuinely nonrecurring restructuring charge appears to remain in the anchor history
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.993 million pretax and $3.059 million after tax in 2025; another $1.503 million was incurred in first-half 2026 and $2-$3 million is anticipated for full-year 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: If genuinely nonrecurring, the charge depresses the 2025 OE observation and therefore the fitted OE trend; it does not enter the selected anchor dollar for dollar because the anchor is the lower trend value rather than latest actual OE.
audit_findings.evidence: One-time costs required to implement the changes in 2025 were approximately $4 million, primarily related to employee severance and other personnel related expenses, and have been substantially incurred and paid during 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The 2025 charge and its inclusion in reported earnings are demonstrated, but its eligibility for normalization is not. The latest filing shows the same program continuing into 2026, contradicting the premise that the economic cost ended in 2025. Even treating the full $3.059 million after-tax amount as a permanent direct uplift to the $31.5 million anchor—an intentionally conservative upper-bound sensitivity—would add about $42.9 million, or $2.49 per share, to base value and leave it near $30.63 versus the $94.62 market price. The actual log-trend effect would be smaller, so the conclusion would not change.
audit_findings.action: Do not normalize the charge now. Track total program costs through completion and rerun the historical OE trend only if later filings establish that comparable footprint and integration charges do not recur.
